intro: A Brooklyn post-punk trio on Captured Tracks.
story: B Boys formed in Brooklyn in 2014 as a trio of Britton Walker, Brendon Avalos and Andrew Kerr; Walker and Avalos met in Denton, Texas, and Kerr is from Florida. They signed to Captured Tracks in 2015, and Exclaim called them a band to watch, citing Wire-like swampy riffs. Kerr has said he works Haitian and Latin American rhythms, like compas, cumbia and bossa nova, into the band. Dada came out in 2017 and Dudu followed, and they played Pickathon in 2019.

intro: A Brooklyn band with sharp, wry art-punk.
story: Bodega is a Brooklyn five-piece led by Ben Hozie and Nikki Belfiglio, formed in 2016 from the ashes of their earlier band Bodega Bay. Endless Scroll, their debut on What's Your Rupture?, came out on July 6, 2018, produced by Austin Brown of Parquet Courts, and NME called them New York's most exciting band after SXSW, as The Guardian relayed. They played Pickathon in 2019. Broken Equipment followed in 2022, Our Brand Could Be Yr Life in 2024 and All Inside Aquarium in 2026.

intro: A vintage-minded roots songwriter.
story: Colton Turner is an Austin rockabilly and honky-tonk songwriter, and his brother Zane plays guitar. Saving Country Music said he made one of the biggest impressions on roots fans at Pickathon 2019, and he filmed an episode of Pickathon's On the Farm series, season 7's Who's Blue, which American Songwriter covered. In November 2026 he released the single "U" with Theo Lawrence.

intro: Old-time fiddle and banjo, played as a duet.
story: David Bragger and Susan Platz are a Los Angeles old-time fiddle duo; Bragger runs the Old-Time Tiki Parlour label, and Platz found her old-time fiddling in one of his workshops. King's Lament: Old-Time Fiddle Duets came out on Tiki Parlour in February 2018, billed as the first American old-time fiddle duet CD. They played Pickathon in 2019, and both have kept teaching and playing at folk gatherings since, including the Alabama Folk School in 2026.

intro: A Washington, D.C. trio of wiry post-punk.
story: Flasher is a Washington, D.C., trio of lifelong locals Taylor Mulitz, Emma Baker and Daniel Saperstein, with a self-titled EP on Sister Polygon in 2016. Constant Image came out on Domino on June 8, 2018, recorded in New York with the producer Nicolas Vernhes; Stereogum made it Album of the Week, and Rolling Stone called it one of 2018's surprisingly excellent debuts. They played Pickathon in 2019. Love Is Yours came out on Domino in 2022 after Saperstein left, and the In My Myth EP in 2023.

intro: San Antonio cosmic country with a honky-tonk streak.
story: Garrett T. Capps is a San Antonio songwriter and former doom-metal and punk drummer who fronts NASA Country and co-owns The Lonesome Rose. One of his songs opened the third season of Billions on Showtime after Spotify playlisting, and he has said an algorithm changed his life. He played Pickathon in 2019, and in 2021 released the single "I Like Austin, But I Love San Antone."

intro: A North Carolina songwriter with a Southern gothic streak.
story: H.C. McEntire is a Durham, North Carolina, native who played in the punk band Bellafea and then fronted Mount Moriah before going solo. Lionheart, her solo debut, came out on Merge in 2018; Pitchfork and Paste both reviewed it, and Spectrum Culture called it a stunning solo debut. She came to Pickathon in 2019, and Eno Axis followed on August 21, 2020 and Every Acre in 2023.

intro: A Portland noise-punk trio.
story: Help is a Portland band that includes And And And's Bim Ditson, and earlier in 2019 it was voted first in Willamette Week's Best New Band poll. A last-minute addition to the Pickathon lineup, it played that August. In October 2024 the band released the six-song EP Courage.

intro: A rotating Los Angeles psych ensemble.
story: JJUUJJUU is a rotating Los Angeles psych ensemble led by Phil Pirrone, whose first EP, FRST, came out in 2013. Zionic Mud, the debut LP, followed in 2018, and they toured opening for Primus, Mastodon, Kikagaku Moyo and Earthless, with festival dates that included Pickathon in 2019. They were live on KEXP in August 2024, and in 2026 toured the U.S. with Angine de Poitrine.
artist_reel_line: Zionic Mud, their debut LP, came out in 2018.

intro: An Australian songwriter of quiet heartbreak.
story: Julia Jacklin was born on August 30, 1990, in the Blue Mountains of New South Wales, Australia. Crushing, her second album, came out on February 22, 2019, and Rolling Stone's headline said she makes her breakthrough with it. She played Pickathon that summer. PRE PLEASURE followed in 2022, and in September 2026 she released The Gem on 4AD.

intro: Jupiter Bokondji's Congolese funk-rock from Kinshasa.
story: Jupiter Bokondji was born in Kinshasa on December 16, 1963, and came to wider notice in the 2006 documentary Jupiter's Dance. Hotel Univers came out in 2013 and Kin Sonic in 2017 with Damon Albarn, Warren Ellis and Robert Del Naja guesting; The Guardian reviewed it as edgy funk with stuttering Kinshasa rhythms, and PopMatters called it adrenaline-fueled. They played Pickathon in 2019. Na Kozonga followed, and Ekoya in 2025.

intro: A Portland rapper and a fixture of the city's underground.
story: Karma Rivera is a Portland rapper of Puerto Rican descent who moved from Chicago to Vancouver, Washington, as a teenager; she did not pick up a mic until she was 20 and has rapped since 2014. Her album I Need to Start a Garden came out in March 2018 and led to a months-long tour of the U.S. and Europe, per Portland Monthly. She played Pickathon in 2019. In 2025 she received the Trailblazer Award at the Star Awards during Portland Hip Hop Week.

intro: A singer with a candid, rock-edged country voice.
story: Lauren Morrow grew up in Georgia and for more than a decade was the lead singer of the Whiskey Gentry, then moved to Nashville around 2017 to go solo. Her Lauren Morrow EP came out on October 12, 2018, recorded at Creative Workshop with Parker Cason, and Saving Country Music praised her earnest songwriting steeped in country roots around Pickathon 2019. People Talk followed in 2023.

intro: Jess Wolfe and Holly Laessig's tightly woven harmonies.
story: Jess Wolfe and Holly Laessig met in 2005 as Berklee students, moved to Ditmas Park, Brooklyn, in 2007 and founded Lucius; the band moved to Los Angeles in 2015. Wildewoman came out on Mom + Pop on October 15, 2013, and Good Grief, made with the producer Shawn Everett, on March 11, 2016. Wolfe told Rolling Stone that after Wildewoman, "all of a sudden we were gone 300 days out of the year." They played Pickathon in 2019. Second Nature followed in 2022 and Lucius in 2025.

intro: A Montana songwriter, with the guitarist Jon Neufeld.
story: Martha Scanlan is a Montana singer-songwriter and old-time musician with four solo albums and one collaboration with the Portland producer Jon Neufeld. She played Pickathon in 2019 with Neufeld, and the two have kept playing together. In August 2026 they toured the Pacific Northwest with Amy Helm.

intro: Tuareg guitar from Niger.
story: Mdou Moctar was born Mahamadou Souleymane near Tchintabaraden, Niger, and is based in Agadez; he taught himself guitar partly from Eddie Van Halen videos, and his music first spread through West African cell-phone trading. Ilana: The Creator, on Sahel Sounds in 2019, brought a wider audience, the year they played Pickathon. Louder profiled him as the Hendrix of the Sahara. Afrique Victime followed on Matador on May 21, 2021, Funeral for Justice in 2024, and an all-acoustic version, Tears of Injustice, in early 2025.

intro: Road-tested Texas honky-tonk from Austin.
story: Mike and the Moonpies are an Austin honky-tonk band led by Mike Harmeier, active since 2007; his first paid gig was a weekly Wednesday set at 14 at the Prairie Rose saloon in Decker Prairie, Texas. Steak Night at the Prairie Rose came out on February 2, 2018, produced by Adam Odor, and reached number 22 on Billboard's Heatseekers chart; Rolling Stone called it a contender for the year's best country album. Harmeier has said the title song is a nod to that first gig, when his dad booked every show he played at 14. Cheap Silver & Solid Country Gold followed in 2019, the year of their Pickathon set, and they made their Grand Ole Opry debut on September 6, 2022. In January 2024 they renamed the band Silverada, and in 2026 they released Living Proof under it.

intro: An LA songwriter with a commanding voice.
story: Miya Folick was raised in Santa Ana, California, trained as a classical singer and is now in Los Angeles; she was first noticed through the 2015 EP Strange Darling and the 2017 EP Give It To Me. Premonitions, her debut album, came out on Terrible and Interscope on October 26, 2018, co-produced with Justin Raisen and Yves Rothman, and Paste praised her jaw-dropping vocal range. She played an NPR Tiny Desk Concert and Pickathon in 2019. Roach followed on Nettwerk in 2023 and Erotica Veronica in February 2025, with a deluxe edition in 2026.

intro: Denver soul-rock with a big band behind it.
story: Nathaniel Rateliff was born in St. Louis and built his career in the Denver folk scene; he formed the Night Sweats in 2013 with the bassist Joseph Pope III and the drummer Patrick Meese, and was 36 when the band began touring in 2015. The self-titled debut came out on Stax on August 21, 2015, and was certified gold in 2017; Tearing at the Seams followed on March 9, 2018. They played Pickathon in 2019. The Future came out on November 5, 2021, and at Newport Folk in 2022 the band staged an American Tune Revue with a surprise appearance by Paul Simon.

intro: A Vancouver Island songwriter of shadowy, psychedelic folk.
story: Ora Cogan was raised on an island in the Salish Sea in British Columbia, joined the Vancouver experimental scene at 19 and is now based in Nanaimo. Shadowland, co-produced by Trish Klein of the Be Good Tanyas, came out in April 2016 and Crickets in November 2017. She played Pickathon in 2019, and Formless followed in 2023. Hard Hearted Woman, her tenth album and Sacred Bones debut, came out on March 13, 2026, and The Tyee profiled her that April as a musician and environmental activist.

act: Phil Lesh & The Terrapin Family Band
intro: The Grateful Dead's co-founder, with his family band.
story: Phil Lesh joined the Warlocks in 1965 at Jerry Garcia's request and became a founding member and bassist of the Grateful Dead; Garcia once said that when Phil's happening, the band's happening. He later toured with a rotating cast as Phil Lesh and Friends, and led the Terrapin Family Band with his sons, playing out of Terrapin Crossroads, the club he opened in Marin County. They played Pickathon in 2019. Lesh died on October 25, 2024, at 84, two days after MusiCares named the Grateful Dead its Persons of the Year.

intro: Portland dream-pop with analog synths and sci-fi imagery.
story: Reptaliens is the Portland duo of Cole and Bambi Browning, a married couple who met filming a music video for a band that did not exist yet. FM-2030, their debut, came out on Captured Tracks in 2017, and they toured in 2017 and 2018 with STRFKR, Cults and of Montreal. Valis, recorded at Jackpot in Portland, followed in 2019, the year of their Pickathon set, and Multiverse in January 2022.

intro: Eva Moolchan's sparse, minimalist post-punk.
story: Eva Moolchan, of Washington, D.C., started Sneaks while studying at the Maryland Institute College of Art in Baltimore. Gymnastics came out in 2016, later reissued, and It's a Myth in 2017. Highway Hypnosis came out on Merge on January 25, 2019, and The Nation profiled her as D.C.'s DIY maverick; she played Pickathon that summer. Happy Birthday followed on Merge on August 21, 2020, and The Eva EP in 2022.

intro: A Portland post-punk and dark-wave band.
story: Tobias Grave founded Soft Kill in San Diego in 2010 as an extension of his one-man band Blessure Grave, and its debut, An Open Door, came out in 2011. The band re-emerged in Portland in 2014, and later he moved to Chicago. Heresy came out in 2015, Choke, on Profound Lore and mixed by Ben Greenberg, in 2016, and Savior on Profound Lore on May 11, 2018. They played Pickathon in 2019.
artist_reel_line: Savior, on Profound Lore, came out on May 11, 2018.

intro: Brothers Colton and Zane Turner.
story: The Mellows are the brothers Colton and Zane Turner, a rockabilly act that played Pickathon in 2019. Talkhouse filmed them performing "A Thousand Kisses."

intro: Songs in honor of Richard Swift.
story: The Richard Swift Hex Band was a one-time tribute set to Richard Swift, the Oregon songwriter and producer, backed by Foxygen's Jonathan Rado, Dr. Dog's Eric Slick and members of Pure Bathing Culture, with Damien Jurado among the singers. Swift died in the summer of 2018, and his final album, The Hex, came out on Secretly Canadian on September 21, 2018. Willamette Week called the August 2019 tribute the best distillation of the Pickathon spirit. In July 2022 Nathaniel Rateliff and the Black Keys honored Swift on stage at Red Rocks.

intro: A band with a Texas touch.
story: The Tender Things is the Austin project of Jesse Ebaugh, a former bassist of the Heartless Bastards who moved from Cincinnati to Austin in 2008. Ebaugh has said he had played on many records but had made nothing of his own, so he started writing songs. The self-titled debut came out in 2018, and the band played Pickathon in 2019. That Texas Touch, the third LP, followed in 2023, and in October 2026 they released The Tender Things Is a Nasty Band.

intro: A hard-driving Asheville bluegrass band.
story: Town Mountain is a bluegrass band from Asheville, North Carolina, founded by Robert Greer and Jesse Langlais, with a honky-tonk streak. They won an IBMA Momentum Award in 2013 and returned to Pickathon in 2019, their fourth visit after 2009, 2010 and 2016. Lines in the Levee, their seventh LP, came out on New West in 2022.

intro: A Swedish band of deadpan, scuzzy punk.
story: Viagra Boys formed in Stockholm in 2015, fronted by the American-born Sebastian Murphy. Street Worms, their debut, came out on YEAR0001 on September 28, 2018, and they played Pickathon in 2019. Welfare Jazz followed in 2021, Cave World in 2022 and viagr aboys in 2025 on their own Shrimptech Enterprises label.

intro: A British duo of art-pop and synths.
story: Virginia Wing is a British art-pop band of Alice Merida Richards and Sam Pillay. Ecstatic Arrow came out on Fire Records on June 8, 2018, recorded at a family home in Switzerland, and they played Pickathon the next summer. private LIFE followed in 2021.

intro: An old-time duo of Appalachian harmony.
story: Vivian Leva and Riley Calcagno were both raised by parents immersed in old-time and bluegrass, and both also play in The Onlies. Leva's solo debut, Time Is Everything, drew Rolling Stone praise in 2018. The duo played Pickathon in 2019 and again in 2022, and their self-titled album, produced by Joel Savoy, came out on Free Dirt on March 12, 2021. They now perform together as Viv and Riley.

intro: A Eugene, Oregon doom trio of slow, crushing weight.
story: YOB formed in Eugene, Oregon, in 1996 around the singer-guitarist Mike Scheidt and the bassist Aaron Rieseberg, and split from 2006 to 2008. Clearing the Path to Ascend came out on Neurot in 2014. Our Raw Heart, their eighth album and first for Relapse, came out on June 8, 2018, and Rolling Stone called YOB perhaps the 21st century's most critically acclaimed doom metal band. They played Pickathon in 2019, Scheidt's second visit after the metal supergroup VHÖL in 2016.
